description: Representation-native long-horizon rest stability under contact. The system's native stable-identity body rests on the system's own released static support (stationary material, floor plane, or equivalent) under its native gravity, for a long rollout. After a declared settling prefix the body must be statically stable: the center of mass stays put up to a small drift bound scaled by the body's own size, the stable-identity shape metrics stay bounded, the state stays finite, and element identity/count never changes. This measures contact stability, creeping drift, and jitter growth over a horizon much longer than the impact-scale scenes.

pass_criteria.quantity: post-settling center-of-mass drift and stable-identity shape boundedness under sustained contact

provenance.reference_formula: for frames after settle_frac of the rollout: max ||x_com(t) - x_com(t_settle)|| <= tail_com_drift_max_rel * L, with L = cbrt(bbox_volume at frame 0) the body's own length scale
regime_assumptions: the support is part of the system's released pipeline, not an adapter-side constraint
native gravity is on for the entire rollout
stable identity: the same physical element keeps the same index in every frame
the drift bound is evaluated only after the declared settling prefix; the transient is unconstrained except for finiteness
provenance.notes: Frozen v1. Submission contract is triangle_metrics.csv exactly as SPEC 2.6 plus the bbox_volume column (already emitted by the released GASP adapter) used solely for the body length scale. A natural controlled fault is an over-aggressive shape-control threshold: sustained contact deformation makes the clamp fire continuously and the shape metrics leave their bounds.
